First, the scenario: My brother, who's 30, moved back in with our parents two years ago after going back to school. I'm 21, in my third year of university, working to put myself through business school, which is tough but manageable. I plan to graduate in two years. I started saving from my paychecks, sometimes as much as 15%, other times as low as 1%, to go on a big vacation after graduation. The fund is now $2800, and I was planning to use it for a cruise, Japan, or a trip to Europe. My brother hasn't been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. Our parents already help him financially, so he wouldn't ask them for more. Last week, when he was complaining to our parents about needing a vacation, they mentioned my vacation fund and suggested he could start saving now to maybe go somewhere in a year. He said since I won't need it for another two years, there's plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about the same as I do but always seems broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (I don't pay rent either, which is why I could build up the fund). I buy most of my groceries, makeup, health supplies, phone, and uni fees. He's mad at me for saying no. He says it's not fair because as the youngest, I get to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he moved out and was older. He says it's not fair that I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went, whereas he had to go back. He says I've only been able to save so much money because mom and dad spoiled me. I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes, taught me to budget. I think my parents spoiled him because he doesn't know how to do much for the real world outside his job. I don't think it's fair for me to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he'll be able to pay me back on time, even if he could. I'm uncomfortable. So, is it AITA for me to refuse to loan my brother my vacation money? He's not good with money, as evidenced by his inability to save despite having a job. 3. **Parents' Involvement**: They suggested he could start saving now, implying they support his need for a vacation but also think he should handle it himself. They mentioned my fund, which might have led him to ask me. 4. **Brother's Arguments**: He feels it's unfair that I have this money while he doesn't. He's upset about past situations where he had to take on more responsibilities earlier in life. He's also accusing me of being spoiled, which I don't agree with. 5. **My Reasoning for Saying No**: I don't trust his ability to pay back the loan, given his history with money. I also feel that my savings are for my future, and it's not my responsibility to fund his vacation. 6. **Emotional Impact**: He's angry, which is making me uncomfortable. I might feel guilty for refusing, but I also stand by my decision. Now, considering whether I'm being unreasonable or if my refusal is justified. On one hand, I have a right to my savings. He's also in a position to start saving now if he wants to go on a vacation in the future. On the other hand, family support is important. However, I don't feel it's my duty to support him financially, especially when he's capable of handling his own money and has other avenues for help. My savings are for me, and I have the right to protect them. I also need to consider the practicality of him paying me back. If he's bad with money, it's a risk. I could end up losing the money, which would be a significant setback for me. In terms of fairness, I don't think it's fair for me to give up my vacation money. I've earned it and saved it responsibly. My brother's resentment seems to stem from past issues, not just this specific request. It's possible that he's projecting his frustrations about his own financial situation onto me. I also don't think I'm being spoiled. I've worked hard and budgeted carefully. My parents have helped me, but I've also contributed to my savings. So, putting it all together, I don't think I'm being unreasonable. My refusal is justified because the money is for my future, I don't trust his ability to repay, and it's not my responsibility to fund his vacation when he has other options and support. Therefore, I don't think I'm AITA in this situation.
